title: subpoena-witness line
description: One line of subpoena-witness output: one exec as the kernel saw it, one send from a session cgroup, or a record that opens or closes a capture window. A line with a record field is a record, one with a delivery_op field a send, and any other line an exec. See docs/ports.md (W, W8). Readers ignore fields they do not know; existing fields keep their name and meaning.

time.description: When the exec or send was seen (for a send, when the witness read it), or the record written (RFC 3339, UTC).

pid.description: PID in the process's own PID namespace.

ppid.description: Parent PID in the process's own PID namespace.

host_pid.description: PID in the initial PID namespace.

comm.description: Kernel task name, at most 15 bytes.

exe.description: The path passed to execve; may be relative.

cgroup.description: cgroup path without the hierarchy root, root-most first, at most 8 elements, such as subpoena/<trace id>.

trace_id.description: The session's trace ID, read from its cgroup name. Present only for execs and sends inside a session cgroup.

attribution.description: How the line was tied to trace_id. Present exactly when trace_id is.

record.description: start: the witness is attached and capturing. stop: it has stopped; healthy says whether the capture between start and stop is complete.

healthy.description: On a stop record: true only if no kernel events were lost and no read or write failed.

error.description: On an unhealthy stop record: what went wrong.

coverage.description: On a stop record: what the capture might have missed even when healthy, in one line.

delivery_op.description: deliver: a send on a connected socket, to the peer the socket holds. sendmsg: a send that named its destination.

protocol.description: tcp, udp, or another IP protocol name or number.

peer.description: The far end of the send as address:port ([address]:port for IPv6). Empty when the witness could not read it: such a send may have gone to any peer.

local.description: This end of the socket, in the same form; empty when unknown.

bytes.description: Bytes the caller asked to send, not bytes the peer received.
